description: Space Dogs is a Panama-based, student-led space technology group focused on research, engineering, and accessible technological solutions. Through its Advanced Research Projects and International Programs (ARPIP) unit, the team develops experimental applications involving aerospace technology, satellite Earth observation, and emerging tools. For the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge, ARPIP is applying NISAR radar data to a geospatial exploration platform focused on Panama
summary:
ISTMOSAR — Vigía del Istmo is a web application under development by Space Dogs (ARPIP) for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. Its objective is to make NASA-ISRO NISAR L-band radar observations over Panama easier to explore through an accessible geographic interface.

The project uses three NISAR Level-2 Geocoded Polarimetric Covariance (GCOV) acquisitions dated 16 June, 28 June, and 14 October 2026. The initial processing focuses on the Frequency A HHHH measurement. The application is designed to let users explore acquisition information, inspect radar imagery, and compare observations through a browser without requiring specialist software or downloading the original large HDF5 files.

ISTMOSAR emphasizes traceable data sources, documented processing, and transparent scientific limitations. Visual differences between acquisitions are not treated as confirmed environmental changes. Quantitative difference products and statistics will be presented only when the relevant data-quality, spatial-compatibility, and scientific-review requirements have been satisfied.
details:
ISTMOSAR — Vigía del Istmo

Project Concept

ISTMOSAR — Vigía del Istmo is a browser-based geospatial application developed by Space Dogs, through its Advanced Research Projects and International Programs (ARPIP) department, for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge challenge “Dancing with the SARs.”

The project addresses an accessibility problem: authentic NISAR Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) products are distributed in technical scientific formats that can be difficult for students, educators, and researchers to inspect without specialized software and substantial data-processing resources.

ISTMOSAR provides an accessible interface for exploring selected NASA–ISRO NISAR observations in a Panama-focused geographic context. The displayed geographic extent is provisional and is not an approved watershed or scientific study-area boundary.

How the Application Works

Users access a public website containing an interactive map, an acquisition catalogue, radar previews, metadata, and a two-date visual comparison interface.

The application currently presents three authentic NISAR Level-2 Geocoded Polarimetric Covariance (GCOV) acquisitions:

  • June 16, 2026 — Cycle 023, Track 040, Frame 084, Forecast orbit fidelity.
  • June 28, 2026 — Cycle 024, Track 040, Frame 084, Near Real-Time orbit fidelity.
  • October 14, 2026 — Cycle 033, Track 040, Frame 084, Near Real-Time orbit fidelity.

The displayed radar channel is Frequency A HHHH. Users can select acquisitions, inspect metadata, control radar-layer visibility and opacity, and visually compare two dates using an interactive crossfade.

Data Processing and Scientific Method

The original NISAR GCOV products were processed locally. The web previews were prepared from Stage 2 HHHH GeoTIFFs containing gamma-zero linear-power measurements.

The preview workflow consists of:

  1. Reading HHHH gamma-zero linear-power data.
  2. Reprojecting and average-resampling the linear values for web visualization.
  3. Converting positive resampled values to decibels using 10 log10.
  4. Applying a shared grayscale display stretch across the three acquisitions.
  5. Exporting lightweight transparent PNG previews for the public application.

The previews are approximately 190 m per pixel and are intended for visualization. They do not replace the original 10 m source measurements. Product quality masks are not applied to these previews.

Scientific Review and Limitations

The three acquisitions have been catalogued, and their exploratory previews have been visually verified. Their raster grids have also been examined for spatial compatibility.

The GCOV mask definitions have been reviewed against the applicable NISAR Level-2 GCOV Product Specification, Revision F. Full-scene raster-value and mask distributions have been inspected.

However, the previously examined upstream QA sidecar candidates were HTML responses rather than valid PDF, HDF5, and CSV QA products. Further ASF QA-sidecar recovery and local NISARQA execution remain outstanding.

The study-area geometry has not received final approval. No approved common-valid-pixel policy or pairwise scientific acceptance has been established. All three candidate temporal pairs remain pending.

Consequently, the application currently supports exploratory observation and visual comparison only. It does not generate or publish accepted quantitative difference rasters or change statistics. A change in radar backscatter alone cannot establish flooding, inundation, deforestation, or another specific environmental event.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ISTMOSAR lowers the technical barrier to exploring satellite radar observations. It provides a public, lightweight interface that can help students, educators, and researchers understand NISAR data, inspect acquisition information, and learn how radar observations are used in Earth science.

Its Panama-focused context demonstrates how international Earth-observation resources can be explored for locally relevant environmental research and education.

Technology and Tools

  • HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript for the web application.
  • Leaflet for interactive geographic visualization.
  • OpenStreetMap for the basemap.
  • JSON for acquisition metadata and application configuration.
  • Python and geospatial processing tools for local data preparation.
  • PNG for lightweight radar-preview display assets.
  • Git and GitHub for version control and source-code management.
  • GitHub Pages for public hosting.
  • Visual Studio Code for development.

Original HDF5 products and full-size processing rasters are kept outside the public website repository. The repository contains the application source code, metadata, and lightweight preview assets.

Creativity and Design Considerations

ISTMOSAR combines authentic satellite radar observations, acquisition metadata, geographic context, and interactive visualization in a single public interface.

The development prioritizes data provenance, traceability, accessibility, mobile usability, application performance, responsible scientific interpretation, and transparent communication of uncertainty.

The application is an exploratory educational and research interface, not an operational flood-monitoring or early-warning system.

Project Team

  • José Peñalba — Technical Director and Lead Developer.
  • Maryfer Higuera — Scientific Data Lead and Frontend Engineer.
  • Tomás Strandgard — UX Reviewer, Quality Assurance, and Documentation.

Space Dogs — Advanced Research Projects and International Programs (ARPIP), Panama.

Project Repositories and File Storage

ISTMOSAR project files, supporting documentation, presentation materials, screenshots, and related working resources are organized through Google Drive and GitHub.

Google Drive — Project File Repository

Purpose: Centralized storage for project documentation, scientific evidence, application screenshots, presentations, research references, and administrative records.

Shared project folder:

https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1RScMHpcGpq0q3cAkm0ADKLG7ndSOSNA4?usp=sharing

Google Drive is used to organize and share project materials among the Space Dogs / ARPIP team.

GitHub — Source Code Repository

Project: ISTMOSAR — Vigía del Istmo

Repository:

https://github.com/akabyn5/ISTMOSAR-Vigia-del-Istmo

Live application:

https://akabyn5.github.io/ISTMOSAR-Vigia-del-Istmo/

GitHub contains the application's HTML, CSS and JavaScript source code, scene metadata, lightweight radar previews, documentation, and deployment configuration. GitHub Pages provides public access to the deployed application.

Resource roles

  • Google Drive: Project files, scientific documentation, evidence packages, screenshots, presentations, and internal working materials.
  • GitHub: Application source code, version history, public documentation, and deployment.
  • GitHub Pages: Public demonstration of the working ISTMOSAR application.

Access verification

Before sharing these resources with reviewers, verify that the Google Drive folder is accessible to the intended audience using its sharing permissions. The GitHub repository and deployed website should also open without authentication requirements.
